findings.title: Usage-limit resume now matches the ACP "app-owned wake turn" predicate
findings.body: `createdBy: "agent"` plus `creationSource: "server"` is exactly what `acpIsAppOwnedWakeTurn` tests (`packages/provider-acp/src/server/adapter.ts:1497-1502`). That predicate is documented as "a delegated child finishing". At `adapter.ts:7914-7917` it skips resetting `midTurnUnreportedCompletedTaskIds`, which a real user turn does reset. A usage-limit auto-resume on an ACP provider therefore stops clearing that set, as a user-typed resume used to. Was this considered? The Pi, Muse, OpenCode and Claude adapters only match `creationSource === "provider"`, so they are unaffected. I did not trace what the set controls, so the impact may be nil.

contracts.action: Usage-limit auto-resume message is now sent as createdBy "agent" (creationSource "server") instead of "user", so the UI attributes it to T3 Code
contracts.equivalent_path: RestartContinuation.ts:326 already dispatches a server-originated "Continue where you left off" with createdBy "agent". client-runtime/src/userMessage.ts:110-115 maps agent+server to the "t3code" attribution.
contracts.before_after: Before, createdBy "user" made the message render as the user's own and count as a user turn. Now it is attributed to T3 Code. The follow-up gate `mayStartSubagentFollowup` (Orchestrator.ts:704-708) and the sender check in `recordSubagentFollowup` (Orchestrator.ts:8046-8049) both accept `usageLimitContinuationOfRunId`, so a subagent child's auto-resume still registers a parent follow-up task, as it did when createdBy was "user". The dispatch guard at Orchestrator.ts:5524-5566 runs before follow-up recording and returns without a message when stale, so `recordSubagentFollowup` exits at `message?.runId == null`. Other createdBy=="user" readers now treat the resume as non-user: ProjectionStore.ts:1572 (latest user-authored time), threadHistoryPaging.ts:300 (user turns), ProviderRuntimeRecoveryService.ts:369 (retryable held messages), ProviderUsageAnalytics.ts:212 (request kind "agent"), and Orchestrator.ts:2465 (a held run for this message counts as unattended and is released). Orchestrator.ts:5685 (title regeneration for user messages after maintenance-only history) and the ACP predicate noted in the finding are the other readers.
contracts.visible_effect: The resume bubble shows the T3 Code attribution instead of looking user-authored. Analytics report it as an agent request rather than a user request.
contracts.failure_mode: If the Orchestrator allow-list were missed, a resumed child would not get a parent follow-up task. Both gates are updated, and the new DelegatedCompletionDelivery test covers that path. On rejection the dispatch emits a metadata-updated no-op, and the sweep's catchCause logs a warning.

summary: The change is small and consistent. The auto-resume message is now sent as createdBy \"agent\" with creationSource \"server\", the same shape `RestartContinuation.ts:326` uses. Both places that decide whether a subagent follow-up gets tracked, `mayStartSubagentFollowup` and the sender check in `recordSubagentFollowup`, now let `usageLimitContinuationOfRunId` through. So a child's auto-resume still registers a parent follow-up task, as it did when createdBy was \"user\". I read the other createdBy==\"user\" readers (history paging, shell latest-user time, runtime recovery retry, analytics, held-run release) and found no breakage. The new tests look sound: the shell snapshot used in the DelegatedCompletionDelivery test includes subagent threads when called without options, and the `createdBy: \"agent\"` assertion in runtimeLayer.test.ts covers the attribution change. I read the code only and did not run the tests. The one low-confidence observation is that the resume now matches the ACP adapter's \"app-owned wake turn\" predicate, which skips a state reset that a user turn performs."
